reason: The hypothesis relies on specific claims about oxide formation and transformation on Q235 steel, but the cited evidence (E1, E2) concerns high-entropy alloy coatings on Q235, not the bare steel itself, and does not address magnetite-to-hematite transformation or salt-corrosion behaviour. No prior evidence is provided for the key premises.
premises: Q235 steel forms a coherent, adherent magnetite (Fe3O4) scale at room temperature in aggressive salt
High-temperature annealing (700–900 °C) transforms magnetite to less protective hematite (Fe2O3) or other oxides
This phase transformation causes scale spallation and accelerated degradation
The cited HEA studies (E1, E2) provide evidence for oxide protection mechanisms applicable to Q235 steel
